assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Each added assertion names a code change that reddens it. test_the_refusal_lists_the_settable_paths_and_the_keyed_forms (:41) hardcodes 'effort_hours', 'status' and the three keyed forms against the message; restoring the bare refusal (raise OpError(f"unsupported plan set path {path!r}")) reddens it. test_the_refusal_reads_the_stores_own_settable_table (:53) iterates _store._PLAN_SET_TOP and asserts each path appears in the message; it reddens if the message restates a stale hardcoded list instead of reading the table, which is the divergence it guards. test_a_near_miss_names_the_settable_path (:62) and test_a_typo_names_the_settable_path_it_is_closest_to (:68) redden if the fold-and-match is removed, which is why the negative-control.log run (bare refusal restored) shows all four failing. test_a_keyed_head_is_not_offered_as_a_bare_settable_path (:79) and test_every_suggested_path_is_one_the_writer_accepts_bare (:90) were added with the repair and redden when the keyed heads are returned to the candidate set, as negative-control.log records (2 failed, 5 passed). The independence caveat is test_every_suggested_path_is_one_the_writer_accepts_bare (:104, assert match.group(1) in _store._PLAN_SET_TOP): the production code computes the suggestion from that same set (reckon/_store.py:2469), so any implementation drawing candidates from _PLAN_SET_TOP satisfies it and it does not verify the suggestion is the nearest. It still catches its own regression — a suggestion of a keyed head such as 'gates' is outside _PLAN_SET_TOP — so it does not survive the change it was added to guard, and durability rests on it only in combination with the named near-miss cases.
